old_findings.note: the final 'operation is not ready' revert of executeBatch is now decoded (as a guard before timestamp[_11] = 1); the in-loop 'underlying transaction reverted' revert, the CallExecuted data and the call data stay raw at copies of mem[64]

regressions.decompiled: _11 = sha3(mem[_9 + 32 len -_9 + t - 32]); timestamp[sha3(mem[_9 + 32 len -_9 + t - 32])]
regressions.old: _11 = sha3(mem[_9 + 32 len mem[_9]]); timestamp[sha3(mem[_9 + 32 len mem[_9]])]
regressions.source: TimelockController.hashOperationBatch: keccak256(abi.encode(targets, values, datas, predecessor, salt))
regressions.issue: The hashed length is now the end-pointer difference with the negative term first, instead of the length word stored on the line before.
regressions.rule: When the length word mem[p] was just stored and not changed, print len mem[p]; otherwise order the sum positive-first (t - p - 32).

improvements: P6 fixed. executeBatch's closing check prints as 'if not _30: revert with 'TimelockController: operation is not ready'' followed by timestamp[_11] = 1, instead of a raw revert after the success path; its dead mapping-key stores are gone.
notes: Diff 80 lines, read in full. 8 while before and after.
summary: Low regression only (negative-first hash length in the operation-id keys); executeBatch's final revert is decoded.
